lead: Five million m² of urban green spaces, twenty kilometres of Blue Flag beaches and four natural parks less than an hour away. Valencia’s nature knows no limits.

Valencia is much more than a city. The capital of the Turia treasures an extraordinarily varied natural setting: from the linear park of the Turia Gardens right in the centre to the coastal lagoon of the Albufera, and from the forests of the Sierra Calderona to the turquoise waters of the Cabriel. All of it within reach, without having to travel more than an hour.
More than 160 kilometres of cycle lanes and a completely flat city make getting around Valencia’s nature easy for any fitness level and any age.

items.title: Urban and wild beaches
items.body: Almost 20 km of Blue Flag beaches. Malvarrosa, Cabanyal, Pinedo and El Saler, the virgin dune beach 10 km from the centre.

items.title: Cycling routes
items.body: More than 160 km of cycle lanes and 40 cycle streets. The Turia Gardens route is the most popular; the Green Ring circles the whole city.

items.title: Hiking in the province
items.body: Routes near Montanejos, the Salto de Chella and the dehesas of Soneja. Inland landscapes less than an hour from the city.

items.title: Starlight astrotourism
items.body: Several municipalities in the province hold Starlight certification. The skies of Ademuz and Requena are ideal for stargazing.

items.title: Adventure sports
items.body: Bungee jumping, climbing, zip lines and canyon descents in natural settings less than an hour from Valencia.

items.title: Biosphere Reserves
items.body: El Maestrat, the Alto Turia and the Sierra del Negrete are biosphere reserves less than two hours away that mass tourism barely knows.

items.title: Turia Gardens
items.body: Valencia’s biggest green lung: nine kilometres of linear park in the old bed of the River Turia, car-free and uninterrupted. It connects the Bioparc and the Parque de Cabecera in the west with the City of Arts and Sciences in the east. Along its route there are sports areas, cafés, the Gulliver Park, the Palau de la Música and numerous historic bridges.
facts: A continuous 9 km cycle lane from the Bioparc to the CAC
Athletics tracks, football pitches and calisthenics areas in the riverbed
The 70 m children’s park built into the garden, free to enter
Sixteen bridges from different eras cross the garden from bank to bank
From the Bioparc to the City of Arts · City centre
Free · Open access all year round

items.title: The Valencian Huerta
items.body: Valencia’s most authentic and least known landscape: the orange groves, vegetable gardens, traditional barracas and historic irrigation channels that have surrounded the city since Moorish times. The huerta is the larder of Valencian cuisine and the origin of paella. The Metropolitan Green Ring runs through this territory on signposted cycling and walking routes.
facts: A circular route of more than 100 km around Valencia’s agricultural belt
The traditional buildings of the Valencian huerta, with thatched roofs
Signposted country tracks for discovering the huerta by bike
Local markets and restaurants working with produce straight from the huerta
Outskirts of the city · Metropolitan green ring

items.title: Valencia Botanical Garden
items.body: The oldest university garden in Spain, founded in 1567, with more than 3,000 plant species from the five continents. A living museum that combines history, science and nature right in the historic centre. Its greenhouses, the umbráculum and the cactus garden are the most singular spaces in this urban oasis next to El Carmen district.
facts: More than 3,000 species from the five continents in a historic garden
Tropical and subtropical flora in climate-controlled spaces
One of the largest collections of cacti and succulents in Spain
Photography and natural science exhibitions in the central building
C/ Quart, 80 · Next to El Carmen district
From €3 · Free with the Tourist Card

items.title: Municipal parks and gardens
items.body: Valencia has almost five million m² of urban green spaces, among them the Jardines de Viveros (with its open-air amphitheatre), the Jardín del Real, the Parque de Cabecera (next to the Bioparc) and the Parque de l’Exposició. A network of urban nature that makes Valencia one of the greenest cities in the Mediterranean.
facts: The park with the open-air amphitheatre where the summer concerts are held
A large park next to the Bioparc with a lake and rest areas in the west of the city
The historic garden of the old royal palace, with a rose garden and a pond
A signposted route past the city’s oldest trees

items.title: L’Albufera Natural Park
items.body: The most important wetland in the Valencian Community and one of the great wetlands of the Peninsula. A freshwater lake of 2,800 hectares surrounded by rice fields, pine woods and dunes, only ten kilometres from the centre of Valencia. The place where Valencian paella was born and the destination of thousands of migratory birds. The sunsets over the lake are unique.
facts: The most authentic experience: crossing the lake in the traditional fishing boat
More than 250 bird species, especially during the migration season
The pine forest between the lake and the sea, with signposted trails
Authentic Valencian paella in the fishing village inside the park
10 km from the centre · Bus 24 and 25
Free entry · Boat from €8 · Bus free with the Tourist Card

items.title: Sierra Calderona Natural Park
items.body: A mountain massif of 47,000 hectares that stretches between the provinces of Valencia and Castellón, only thirty kilometres from the centre. Mediterranean forests of pine and holm oak, ravines, viewpoints and mountain villages such as Serra, Náquera and Estivella. The Pico del Garbí, at 598 metres, offers some of the best views of Valencia and the Mediterranean.
facts: The most popular route: 3 h there and back with panoramic views of the Mediterranean
Trails and forest tracks set up for mountain biking
Serra, Náquera and Estivella: rural architecture and inland cuisine
Equipped routes in different sectors of the massif’s limestone rock
Free entry · By car or public transport

items.title: Turia Natural Park
items.body: The River Turia, before reaching Valencia, runs between Mediterranean forests and limestone ravines in a natural park of almost 20,000 hectares. Chulilla, with its impressive suspension bridge, and the villages of Gestalgar and Bugarra are the most visited destinations. Canyoning, climbing and hiking trails along the riverbed are the star activities.
facts: The wooden bridge over the ravine, one of the most photographed in the province
Descent of the Turia ravine with abseils and crystal-clear pools
Chulilla is one of Spain’s benchmark sport climbing destinations
Signposted routes that follow the river between pools and riverside vegetation
Free entry · Canyoning with a company from €40

items.title: Hoces del Cabriel (Cabriel Gorges)
items.body: The least-known natural treasure of the province of Valencia: the River Cabriel runs between limestone canyons, forming pools of an almost implausibly intense turquoise. Declared a Natural Park in 2021, the Cabriel is the river with the best water quality in Spain. Hiking trails along its banks and canoeing are the most popular activities.
facts: Routes of 2 to 6 hours skirting the gorges and pools of the River Cabriel
Paddle down the river through movie-set landscapes with turquoise water
Crystal-clear water and pleasant temperatures from June to September
The Utiel-Requena district combines nature and quality wine tourism

blocks.title: Tips for enjoying nature in Valencia
items: The Turia Gardens and all municipal parks are free and open to everyone
Bus 24 and 25 go from the centre to the Albufera, free with the Tourist Card
El Saler beach has a public bus link and is the most natural and peaceful
160 km of cycle lanes let you get around the city and the huerta by bike
The Sierra Calderona is 30 min away by car and has free parking at the trailheads
The waters of the Cabriel are at their best colour from May to September
